title: Quarter-Wave Seeded Stack with ±15% Thickness Jitter and Expanded Bounds
scientific_hypothesis: Starting from quarter-wave optical thickness seeds at band centers (375nm UV, 1350nm SWIR) with ±15% random jitter will escape local minima that constrained the chirped parameterization, while expanding thickness bounds to 500nm provides additional design freedom without violating fabrication limits.
design_principle: Quarter-wave stack theory provides optimal reflectance per layer pair; jittering seeds allows optimizer to find non-quarter-wave improvements while maintaining physical intuition. Evidence shows quarter-wave stacks maximize reflectivity for minimum layer count when optical thickness equals λ/4.
proposed_topology: exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers)
design_variables: 30 individual layer thicknesses (nm), each independently optimizable
soft_objectives: Maximize average transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band
Maximize average reflectance in 300-450 nm band
manufacturing_considerations: Individual layer thickness bounds: 20-500 nm (expanded from 450 nm per feedback)
Outermost SiO2 layer >= 200 nm for environmental durability
theory_basis: Quarter-wave stack theory: reflectivity maximizes when layer optical thickness equals λ/4
Outermost low-index layer improves environmental durability per multi-wavelength HR evidence
expected_advantages: Better convergence than monotonicity-constrained chirp due to unconstrained thickness space
Quarter-wave seeds provide physically meaningful starting point
Expanded bounds allow thicker layers for broader UV reflection band
known_risks: May converge to local minimum if jitter amplitude insufficient
30 independent variables may require more optimization iterations
No monotonicity constraint could produce non-fabricable thickness profiles
execution_request_english: Optimize a 30-layer HfO2/SiO2 multilayer coating on fused silica substrate at normal incidence with unpolarized illumination. Stack topology: Air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | ... (alternating, 15 bilayer pairs, 30 total finite layers) | Fused Silica. Initialize layer thicknesses using quarter-wave optical thickness at 375 nm for HfO2 and SiO2 layers in the first 10 pairs (UV reflector region), and at 1350 nm for remaining 5 pairs (SWIR transmitter region). Apply ±15% uniform random jitter to all seed thicknesses. Set individual layer thickness optimization bounds: 20 nm minimum, 500 nm maximum. Constrain outermost SiO2 layer thickness >= 200 nm. Optimize all 30 layer thicknesses simultaneously to maximize average transmittance in 1000-1700 nm band and maximize average reflectance in 300-450 nm band. Use gradient-based optimizer with increased initial population sampling density (2x baseline). Evaluate spectrum from 300-1700 nm at 5 nm resolution. Topology realization override: disregard any symbolic repeat count, range, or ellipsis above and use exactly 6 alternating HfO2/SiO2 pairs (12 finite layers). Optimize only continuous physical thicknesses; the task compiler must fully expand every finite layer. Canonical user controls: wavelength intervals 300-450 nm, 1000-1700 nm. soft objectives: high transmission in 1000-1700 nm; high reflection in 300-450 nm. behaviors to suppress or avoid: low transmission in 300-450 nm; low reflection in 1000-1700 nm. manufacturing constraints: total layer count <= 30; materials restricted to HfO2 and SiO2.
revision_reason: Applied feedback directives: ±15% jitter to quarter-wave seeds, expanded upper thickness bound from 450 nm to 500 nm, increased population sampling density. Removed monotonicity constraint that reduced score from 0.7998 to 0.7148 in prior iteration.
